title: Sorting and comparators
lesson:
Sorting numbers and Strings is easy: they already know their order. But how should Java sort a list of harvests? By kg? By farmer's name? By date? You have to tell it, and there are two ways.

**Comparable: the natural order.** The class itself says how its objects normally compare, by implementing `Comparable<T>` and its one method `compareTo`:

```
class Harvest implements Comparable<Harvest> {
    ...
    @Override
    public int compareTo(Harvest other) {
        return Integer.compare(kg, other.kg);   // negative, zero or positive
    }
}
Collections.sort(list);   // or list.sort(null)
```

The rule: return a **negative** number if `this` comes first, **zero** if they're equal in order, **positive** if `this` comes after. Use `Integer.compare` / `Double.compare` / `a.compareTo(b)`, not subtraction (`kg - other.kg` overflows for huge numbers and fails for doubles).

**Comparator: any order you like, from outside.** A `Comparator<T>` is a separate object that compares two T's. You build them from small parts:

```
Comparator<Score> ranking =
    Comparator.comparingInt(Score::getPoints).reversed()   // most points first
              .thenComparingInt(Score::getSeconds)         // then fastest
              .thenComparing(Score::getPlayer);            // then A to Z
scores.sort(ranking);
```

- `Comparator.comparing(key)` sorts by a key (`comparingInt` / `comparingDouble` for numbers).
- `.reversed()` flips the whole comparator built so far. Put it right after the key you want reversed, before adding tie-breakers.
- `.thenComparing(...)` decides ties.
- `String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER` and `Comparator.reverseOrder()` are ready-made.
- A lambda works too: `(a, b) -> Integer.compare(b.kg, a.kg)`.

**Which one?** Comparable for the one obvious order (by date, by id). Comparators for everything else, especially screens that sort many ways (a leaderboard by points, an inventory by weight or value).

Habits that save you:
- **Always add a tie-breaker** for things shown to people. Without one, two players with equal points can swap places between runs and confuse everyone.
- `list.sort(...)` changes the list itself. If the caller's list must stay as it was, sort a copy: `new ArrayList<>(list)`. And `List.of(...)` can't be sorted in place at all: it throws.
- Sorting is O(n log n); fine for thousands of records. Sorting inside a loop that runs every frame of a game is not.

Real uses: leaderboards, "top 3 crops this season", sorting clinic patients by urgency then arrival time, a robot picking the closest target.

notes: new ArrayList<>(List.of(...)) gives a list we're allowed to sort.
Equal urgency: whoever arrived earlier goes first (thenComparingInt).
The same list sorted a second way with a different comparator.

exercises.title: Natural order for harvests
exercises.prompt: Make Harvest's compareTo order harvests by kg, smallest first (use Integer.compare). In Harvests write static List<Harvest> sorted(List<Harvest> hs) returning a NEW sorted list (the input must not change, and it may be a List.of), and static Harvest biggest(List<Harvest> hs) returning the heaviest, or null if empty. toString is done ("Amina:40").

tests.call: Harvests.sorted(java.util.List.of(new Harvest("Amina", "maize", 40), new Harvest("Juma", "beans", 12), new Harvest("Otieno", "maize", 55)))
Harvests.biggest(java.util.List.of(new Harvest("Amina", "maize", 40), new Harvest("Otieno", "maize", 55), new Harvest("Juma", "beans", 12)))

((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { java.util.List<Harvest> orig = new java.util.ArrayList<>(java.util.List.of(new Harvest("A", "x", 9), new Harvest("B", "x", 1))); Harvests.sorted(orig); return orig.toString(); }).get()
tests.name: input unchanged

hints: sorted: List<Harvest> copy = new ArrayList<>(hs); Collections.sort(copy); return copy;
biggest: if empty return null, else Collections.max(hs).

exercises.title: Leaderboard
exercises.prompt: Score has getPlayer(), getPoints(), getSeconds(). Write static List<String> rank(List<Score> scores) returning player names in leaderboard order: most points first, then fewest seconds, then name A to Z. Build it with Comparator.comparingInt(...).reversed().thenComparing... Don't change the input list. Write static List<String> top(List<Score> scores, int n): the first n names of the ranking (all of them if n is bigger; empty if n <= 0).

tests.call: Leaderboard.rank(java.util.List.of(new Score("Amina", 50, 120), new Score("Juma", 70, 200), new Score("Otieno", 50, 90)))
Leaderboard.top(java.util.List.of(new Score("Amina", 50, 120), new Score("Juma", 70, 200), new Score("Otieno", 50, 90)), 2)

tests.why: Build the order with a Comparator.

hints: Copy, sort, then collect the names: for (Score s : copy) names.add(s.getPlayer());
top: List<String> r = rank(scores); return new ArrayList<>(r.subList(0, Math.max(0, Math.min(n, r.size()))));

exercises.title: Season report
exercises.prompt: Two sorts for a farm report. static List<String> byLength(List<String> names): shortest name first, ties in A to Z order ignoring capitals (String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER). static List<String> topCrops(Map<String, Integer> totals, int n): the n crops with the most kg as "maize 40", biggest first, ties by crop name A to Z; all of them if n is bigger than the map. Don't change the inputs.
hints: topCrops: List<Map.Entry<String, Integer>> es = new ArrayList<>(totals.entrySet()); then sort with a lambda.
es.sort((a, b) -> a.getValue().equals(b.getValue()) ? a.getKey().compareTo(b.getKey()) : Integer.compare(b.getValue(), a.getValue()));

quiz.q: compareTo returns a negative number. That means…
quiz.why: Negative: this first; zero: same place; positive: after.

quiz.q: Why prefer Integer.compare(a, b) to a - b?
choices: Subtraction can overflow and give the wrong sign
points high to low, then names A to Z
points high to low, names Z to A
quiz.why: reversed() applies to what was built before it.
Copy it into an ArrayList first.

quiz.q: Comparable or Comparator for a leaderboard that can sort by points OR by time?
quiz.why: A class has one natural order; extra orders are comparators.

cards.a: Comparable: the class's own natural order (compareTo). Comparator: a separate order object.

cards.q: Sort by a key, biggest first?
Sort without changing the caller's list?

explain: Explain the difference between Comparable and Comparator, using a leaderboard or harvest list you make up. Why does a tie-breaker matter?
